text:
maria: Heads up — p50 sparkline for /v1/generate on the dashboard looks lower than the p50 value in the summary card. noticed on EU canary this morning. :eyes:
ajay: same, saw it too around 07:10 UTC. sparkline dips but p50 number stays flat. maybe sampling mismatch?
sam: could be two different rollups: sparkline uses per-minute rollups, summary uses 1h rollup with tdigest merge?
maria: that was my first thought. but i pulled raw counts and the sample_count on the sparkline query is way lower than expected for a few buckets.
kevin: post the actual queries you ran — we might be double-weighting some samples during route-merge.
maria: pasted the one i ran locally:
```
SELECT
  time_bucket('1m', ts) as minute,
  approx_percentile(latency_ms, 0.5) as p50,
  count(*) as cnt
FROM latency_rollups
WHERE endpoint = '/v1/generate' AND region = 'eu' AND ts >= now() - interval '2h'
GROUP BY minute
ORDER BY minute;
```
lia: if sparkline is using the per-client sampled stream and summary uses composite rollup, that'll explain the number gap. sparkline could be showing only routed-to-canary samples.
ajay: hmm — there was a routing policy tweak yesterday that biases small payloads to fast-path model variants. that changes sample distribution by client (and we tag samples differently).
sam: can we reproduce by forcing the same sample source for both visualizations? e.g., run the sparkline query against the composite rollup table with merge_mode='full'.
kevin: i ran a quick compare. summary p50=42ms, sparkline median spikes to 28ms for a minute window where sample_count=18 while composite_count=120. so small sample windows are misleading.
maria: UX idea: show "sample_count" overlay on the sparkline and a tiny warning badge when count < N (configurable). even a subtle dotted outline would help.
lia: agree. also add a hover that shows rollup source (raw/sampled/merged) + sample_count. we currently hide that metadata.
ajay: long-term, we should unify p50 computation: use merged tdigest for displayed percentiles and only show per-source percentiles as a separate trace. keeps the single-number stable.
kevin: patch proposal: add sample_count thresholds to alerting and show per-route sample provenance in the legend. i can draft the console PR.
sam: quick ops check — any chance routing change is still rolling and creating skew? @deploy-bot any recent routing config deploys?
deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-20T07:02:14Z: routing-service v2.18.1 -> canary (owner: ajay). included change: small-payload routing bias for eu.
maria: OK that matches. action items: (1) kevin -> console hover + sample_count indicator (PR by EOD?) (2) sam -> query change to use merged tdigest for summary (3) ajay -> confirm routing bias rollout window and record client segments affected.
lia: i'll add a quick UX note to the rollout checklist to toggle sample provenance visibility for future rollouts.
ajay: will do, and i'll roll back canary if we see higher-than-expected SLO noise.
maria: thanks all. one more tiny thing: can we add a tiny info tooltip near p50 that says "calculated from X samples (source: merged/composite/raw)" so PMs stop opening tickets? :sweat_smile:
kevin: noted. adding that to the PR.
sam: TL;DR: mismatch caused by sampling source + routing bias; fix=show counts+source in UI and compute single-number from merged rollup.
maria: perfect. closing the thread after PRs link back here. :white_check_mark:
